title: Which Madhhab Fits You Best
description: Explore which school of Islamic law your approach to worship and daily life is closest to.

questions.text: When two hadith appear to differ, what is the best approach?

options.text: Analyze both, then prefer the one supported by qiyas and companions' opinion
Prefer the hadith that aligns with practice of Medina
Reconcile them using usul and give preference to stronger isnad
Take the apparent (zahir) meaning of the stronger hadith

questions.text: When a legal issue has no direct hadith or Quranic text, how should it be addressed?

options.text: Derive through qiyas based on similar cases
Consider maslahah and local custom
Suspend judgment until textual proof appears
Follow the principle of caution (ihtiyat) and the statements of early scholars

questions.text: How should weak hadith be used in legal rulings?

options.text: Can be accepted if supported by qiyas or general principles
Can be used if in harmony with Amal Ahl al-Madina
Should be avoided when stronger hadith exist
Should be used if it has no contradiction and fits the text literally

questions.text: Which best describes your view on qiyas (analogical reasoning)?

options.text: Essential tool to ensure consistency and logic in rulings
Acceptable but secondary to practice and maslahah
Used with strict conditions only when no text exists
Used rarely and with caution, preferring direct texts

questions.text: How do you treat the practice ('amal) of the people of Medina as a source?

options.text: Respected but not binding
Primary proof after Quran and Sunnah
Only accepted if confirmed by hadith
Not considered an independent proof

questions.text: When facing two valid scholarly opinions, how should one choose?

options.text: By evaluating which aligns better with qiyas and logic
By observing what scholars of Medina practiced
By following the one backed by stronger hadith
By adhering to the earlier generation's (Salaf) view
Can define rulings when texts are silent
Has strong influence especially in public matters
Accepted only if consistent with textual evidence
Has minimal effect unless directly mentioned in text

questions.text: In deriving new rulings (ijtihad), what is the key principle?

options.text: Systematic reasoning using established legal principles
Balancing texts with public interest (maslahah)
Strict adherence to methodology of usul al-fiqh
Following the understanding of the Salaf closely

Hanafi.name: Hanafi
Hanafi.description: Your approach aligns with the Hanafi school, which emphasizes systematic reasoning (qiyas) and rational analysis in deriving rulings. The Hanafi madhhab values consistency and logical coherence in Islamic law.

Maliki.name: Maliki
Maliki.description: Your approach aligns with the Maliki school, which gives significant weight to the practice of the people of Medina and considers public interest (maslahah) in legal rulings. The Maliki madhhab balances textual evidence with practical considerations.

Shafi'i.name: Shafi'i
Shafi'i.description: Your approach aligns with the Shafi'i school, which follows a systematic methodology (usul al-fiqh) with strict conditions for accepting evidence. The Shafi'i madhhab emphasizes strong hadith authentication and careful reconciliation of sources.

Hanbali.name: Hanbali
Hanbali.description: Your approach aligns with the Hanbali school, which prioritizes direct textual evidence and the understanding of the early generations (Salaf). The Hanbali madhhab takes a cautious approach to analogical reasoning and emphasizes literal meanings of texts.
